questions.q: How many legs does an adult spider have?
questions.a: Eight. Count four pairs.

questions.q: Which two body features help you tell a spider from an adult insect?
questions.a: A spider has eight legs and two main body sections. An adult insect has six legs and three main sections.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its bright rings?
questions.a: Saturn. Its rings are wide enough to see with a small telescope.

questions.q: What are most of the particles in Saturn’s rings made of?
questions.a: Water ice. Sunlight reflecting from the ice makes the rings look bright.

questions.q: Which part of a plant is a carrot: a root, leaf or flower?
questions.a: A root. The part we usually eat grows underground.

questions.q: Which spice comes from the bark of a tree?
questions.a: Cinnamon. Thin strips of bark curl as they dry.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.a: Four. Players usually draw a bow across them.

questions.q: Which is the lowest-pitched instrument in a standard string quartet?
questions.a: The cello. A string quartet has two violins, one viola and one cello.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.a: Six. A honeycomb cell is a familiar example.

questions.q: What is the smallest prime number greater than ten?
questions.a: Eleven. Its only positive divisors are one and eleven.

questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.a: The Pacific. It lies between the Americas and Asia and Australia.

questions.q: What kind of water forms where a freshwater river mixes with seawater?
questions.a: Brackish water. It is saltier than fresh water and less salty than seawater.

questions.q: What does a table of contents help you find?
questions.a: Chapters or sections and where they begin. It is usually at the front.

questions.q: Which part of a reference book lists topics alphabetically with their page numbers?
questions.a: The index. Look for it near the back.

questions.q: How many points is a free throw worth in basketball?
questions.a: One. The player shoots from the free-throw line.

questions.q: A basketball team scores twice from beyond the three-point line and makes one free throw. How many points is that?
questions.a: Seven. Two threes plus one makes seven.

questions.q: What do we call water that freezes and falls from clouds in flakes?
questions.a: Snow. A snowflake is made of ice crystals.

questions.q: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.a: A barometer. Changes in pressure can help forecasters follow weather systems.

questions.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.a: 366. February gets the extra day.

questions.q: Which year was a leap year: 1900 or 2000?
questions.a: 2000. A century year in the Gregorian calendar is a leap year when it is divisible by 400.
